statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail eases one point to 25% at the floor of the elevated band and Stress is high at 69%.
recommendation: Nasdaq-100 futures have stopped extending: a marginal new low at 29,184.25 was rejected and price has recovered to 29,223, about 39 points above the low and roughly 15 points higher than an hour ago. Yields, crude and volatility have each eased marginally from their session extremes, so the amplifier stack is no longer tightening. The retracement is nevertheless shallow at about 12% of the decline, the broken 29,435-29,570 overnight band is unreclaimed and price remains in the lower part of a 386-point range, so the mapped policy state stays at BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES with Tail reduced by one point to 25%. Conditional risk remains concentrated in the narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC window covering the US cash open and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases. The assessment would ease into the WATCH band on a reclaim and hold of 29,330, and would move toward the strong-block band only on a decisive break below 29,184.25 followed by further extension.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures stall at 29,223 after a marginal new low is rejected, while a 4.78% US 10-year, $88 crude and a 15.85 VIX ease slightly off their extremes
body: The second down-leg has stalled. At 10:16 UTC Nasdaq-100 futures traded 29,223.00-29,224.50, about -0.98% and some 289 points below the 29,513 previous close, on a session range of 29,184.25-29,571.25. Two independent quote sources agree on the level and the range. The distinguishing development against the previous hour is that the extension did not continue: the session low was extended only 11 points, to 29,184.25 from 29,195.75, that low was rejected, and price now sits about 39 points above it and roughly 15 points higher than the 29,206-29,211 print at 09:15 UTC. A full hour has passed without a further leg. That is a material change from the 09:00 UTC hour, when repeated extension with the index pinned within 12 points of its low justified raising Tail to 26%. The cross-asset stack has also stopped tightening at the margin. The US 10-year yield is 4.783%, up 2.7 basis points on the day and still the highest since January 2025, but marginally below the 4.79% reading an hour ago, with the 2-year at 4.36%. WTI is $87.64 (+2.20%) and Brent $91.96 (+1.63%), each a little softer than the $87.84 and $92.24 seen at 09:15. VIX is 15.85 (+6.23%) with a session range of 14.95-15.96, so it has come off its high rather than making a new one, and remains low in absolute terms. Reuters reporting continues to attribute the synchronised sovereign selloff to oil-driven inflation pressure, expected central-bank tightening, record sovereign and AI-related corporate issuance and deteriorating fiscal conditions, with Japan's 10-year above 3% for the first time since 1996 and the German 10-year near 3.34%, the highest since 2011. On the geopolitical vector, the Reuters factbox on Kharg Island records that the post claiming the terminal was being destroyed was an AI-generated image, that Iranian officials dismissed it and that US military officials confirmed no such attack occurred, so the specific threat to Iran's principal export hub is a headline rather than a verified physical disruption. Market pricing for a 25 basis-point September hike remains in the 57-65% range after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address. Weighing this, Tail is reduced by one point to 25%. It is not cut further because the bounce retraces only about 12% of the decline, price remains in the lower fifth of the session range, the broken 29,435-29,570 band has not been reclaimed and every amplifier remains directionally aligned even if none is still extending; a shallow pullback within a downtrend is not yet evidence that mean reversion works. It is not held higher because the specific structure that drove the 26% reading, repeated extension with price pinned to the low, has not repeated for a full hour. Stress eases to 69% on the marginal cross-asset stabilisation while remaining high. Confidence is 86% on two cross-verified futures quotes, verified yields, crude and volatility levels, a verified seven-day event calendar and verified current reporting, moderated because tick-level retracement detail is not available. Delayed shared cross-asset context collected at 05:50 UTC is more than four and a half hours old, far beyond the 90-minute freshness bound and predating both down-legs, so it has not been used as evidence for the current price path.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Twenty-two of them mapped to the EA_ON band with Tail between 9 and 13 and Stress climbing steadily from 47 to 58, and dominant mode was mixed in 21 of the 24. The single earlier elevated reading was Tail 11 with mode event/whipsaw in the 10:00 UTC hour on August 31. Through the August 31 US session Stress rose as crude extended on the Larak Island exchange, the 10-year pushed to its highest level since January 2025 and September rate-hike odds firmed after the Jackson Hole address, while Tail stayed compressed because the price path itself remained two-sided. The overnight hours held that pattern with Stress at 50-58 and Tail at 9-11. The break came in the final two lookback hours on September 1: Tail 22 with mode trend-down at 08:00 UTC as the overnight band gave way, then Tail 26 at 09:00 UTC as a second leg extended with price pinned near the session low. The current hour is the first since that break in which the path has not extended further.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is that today's rates-led repricing resolves into two-sided trade rather than a persistent no-retracement path, and the projection now starts from a stalled second leg rather than from an accelerating one. Tail is therefore held at 25% through the European late morning and projected to slip to 24% and the WATCH band in the US pre-market, conditional on no new low. Conditional risk then concentrates in the 13:30-15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open, the final S&P Global Manufacturing PMI and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases, where forecast Tail peaks at 28 and Stress at 76 with mode projected event/whipsaw, still below the strong-block threshold because event dispersion primarily raises Stress. The path is projected to decay from 16:00 UTC as post-release volatility ages, with a modest flow-driven uptick in the 19:00 UTC power hour and an after-hours dispersion checkpoint as Palo Alto Networks, Dell Technologies, Medtronic and MongoDB report. Tail is projected back inside the EA_ON band from 20:00 UTC, reaching its trough near 03:00-04:00 UTC before firming gently with the Tokyo JGB reopen and again into the September 2 European session ahead of ADP. The projection would be invalidated by a decisive break below 29,184.25 followed by further extension, NQ pinning to session lows through the US afternoon, another leg in the global bond rout, or a verified physical disruption to Gulf energy flows.
